propositions: The s3 optional extra must be declared in pyproject.toml as git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 with a guard that validates both presence on PATH and version >= 0.3.2 before use.

A require_s3_helper() function must be added to src/rebar/_optional.py that fails closed (raises OptionalDependencyError with actionable install hint) if the git-remote-s3 console script is missing, the distribution is not installed, the version is too old, or the version string is unparseable.

The version comparison must parse version strings to tuple form (splitting on dot and extracting leading digits from the first three components) without external dependencies, treating non-numeric leading components as failure.
The git_remote_s3 importable module must be probed via importlib.metadata.version() rather than direct import, to keep _optional.py stdlib-only and avoid importing the optional dependency itself.

Unit tests must cover success cases (0.3.2, 0.4.0, 0.3.2.post1), failures (script missing, metadata missing, too old version 0.2.9), and edge cases (unparseable version "unknown") with mocked shutil.which and importlib.metadata.version.
The guard_import() probe for git_remote_s3 with extra="s3" must produce the standard one-line error message containing the exact string pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]' when the module is absent.
